chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created a people, protecting them from affliction. He created them in well-being, gave them life in well-being, caused them to die in well-being, and entered them to die in well-being, and admitted them into Paradise in well-being.

key_terms.عَافِيَةٍ: Well-being, safety, or freedom from harm

ai.seo_question: Who are the people protected from affliction in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), highlighting a distinct category of the faithful who were spared the trials (balā') that test others, thereby preserving their spiritual purity. This complete well-being (ʿāfiyah) spans their entire lifecycle—from creation to death and entry into Paradise—emphasizing divine mercy as a form of protection rather than mere absence of hardship. Shia scholars often interpret this as referring to the Ahl al-Bayt or the most righteous believers whose hearts were shielded from the corrupting effects of suffering.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I heard him<sup>asws</sup> saying that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Created a people, Protecting them from the afflictions. Creating them in good health, and Letting them to live in good health, and Causing them to die in good health, and Entering them into the Paradise in good health’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “I heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) saying, ‘

Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, has created a creature that He is very acquisitively protective of. He has created them in peace and security, grants them life in peace and security, causes them to die in peace and security and will admit them in paradise in peace and security.’”
